task_prompt: Write 1 2 3 4 on the whiteboard with the marker, then erase the 4 with the eraser.
task_summary: The right hand picks up the marker and the left hand the eraser; the right hand writes 1, 2, 3 and 4 in a row on the whiteboard lying on the table; the left hand wipes out the 4 with the eraser; both tools are put back where they came from.

environment.support_surface: white tablecloth on a table; the whiteboard lies flat on it
environment.camera: fixed camera above the operator looking down the table

objects.name: whiteboard

appearance.frame: thin light grey or silver edge

objects.approximate_size: covers most of the near half of the table, about two forearm-lengths wide
properties: A flat rigid panel lying on the table; it does not move during the task.
Marker contact produces visible dark strokes that persist after the tip lifts.
Sliding eraser contact removes the strokes it passes over while strokes it does not touch stay visible.
objects.initial_state: blank, lying flat in the middle of the table
objects.final_state: shows 1, 2 and 3 in a row; the 4 is wiped off
objects.evidence: prompt: 'whiteboard'; the white panel is present in every frame; strokes appear from 8 s and the rightmost one disappears between 15 s and 21 s.

objects.name: black whiteboard marker
properties: A rigid pen held in a writing grip with the tip toward the board.
Moving the tip against the board leaves a visible dark trace; lifting it stops the trace.
It has a cap that is removed before writing and is held in the hand or put back afterwards.
objects.initial_state: lying on the table at the right edge of the board
objects.final_state: lying back at the right edge of the board
objects.evidence: prompt: 'marker'; 4 to 6 s the right hand picks it up from the right; 8 to 14 s its tip traces the digits; 22 to 24 s it is put back on the right.

objects.name: whiteboard eraser
properties: A rigid block held from above with its broad felt face down.
Sliding its wiping face over the board removes the marker strokes it contacts.
objects.initial_state: lying on the table at the left edge of the board
objects.final_state: lying back at the left edge of the board
objects.evidence: prompt: 'eraser'; 6 to 7.5 s the left hand picks it up from the left; 15 to 21 s it is rubbed back and forth over the 4; 22 to 24 s it is put back on the left.

hand_roles.right: Grasps the marker from the right edge of the board and lifts it.

subgoals.goal: The marker is held in the right hand.

hand_roles.left: Grasps the eraser from the left edge of the board and lifts it.

subgoals.goal: The eraser is held in the left hand.

hand_roles.left: Holds the eraser at the left.
hand_roles.right: Pulls the cap off the marker tip.

subgoals.goal: The tip is removed from the cap.

subgoals.action: Write the digit 1 on the board.

hand_roles.left: Holds the eraser away from the board.
hand_roles.right: Moves the marker tip along the stroke in contact with the board.

subgoals.goal: A dark 1 is visible on the board.

subgoals.action: Write the digit 2 to the right of the 1.
Write the digit 3 to the right of the 2.
Write the digit 4 to the right of the 3.

hand_roles.right: Traces the 4, then lifts the marker away.

subgoals.goal: The board displays 1, 2, 3 and 4 in order.

subgoals.action: Wipe repeatedly over the 4 with the eraser.

hand_roles.left: Presses the eraser's felt face on the 4 and slides it back and forth.
hand_roles.right: Holds the marker up, away from the board.

subgoals.goal: The 4 is no longer readable; 1, 2 and 3 remain.

subgoals.action: Put the eraser back at the left edge of the board.

hand_roles.left: Carries the eraser to the left and sets it down.

subgoals.goal: The eraser rests on the table to the left of the board.

subgoals.action: Put the marker back at the right edge of the board.

hand_roles.right: Carries the marker to the right and sets it down, then withdraws.

subgoals.goal: The marker rests on the table to the right of the board.

task_success: The board shows 1, 2, 3 with the 4 erased; the marker lies on the table immediately to the right of the board, and the eraser lies on the table immediately to the left of the board.
notes: Writing is decomposed per digit because each digit is a separate stroke sequence with a checkable outcome.
Recapping the marker is not clearly visible; it is omitted.
